## Finding

For `int f (constexpr int x) { return x; }` the compiler reports error 198, "storage class other
than register specified for parameter", and then terminates with SIGSEGV. This was reproduced for
mcs51 on r17228 with the small and the large model. The compiler crashes when the function returns
the parameter, compares it, converts it to `_Bool`, or adds it to other parameters. It also
crashes when the type of the parameter is a typedef name of a scalar type.

## Cause

The three alternatives of `parameter_declaration` in `src/SDCC.y` report error 198 and leave the
`constexpr` marker in the type specifier of the parameter. `propagateConstExpr` in
`src/SDCCast.c` calls `constExprValue` for operands whose type has the marker, and
`constExprValue` reads the value from `ival`, the initializer of the symbol. Parameters do not
have initializers. `list2val` returns NULL for the null `ival`, and `copyValue` dereferences that
pointer.

## Fix

Each of the three alternatives sets `SPEC_CONSTEXPR` to 0 where it reports the error. After the
error the compiler treats the parameter as an ordinary one. The crash needs only the change to the
first alternative, which is for parameters with names. The two alternatives for parameters without
names clear the marker too, so that the type of every parameter is without the marker after the
error.

The patch in the third comment of the ticket clears the marker at the same three places. Outside
the tests, it has two changes that this patch does not have. It applies the check for error 198 to
the specifier that `getSpec` returns, where r17228 requires `IS_SPEC` of the declaration
specifiers. It also changes `valdiag.py`, which then reports a crash of the compiler as a failure
of the test case.

## Verification

`support/valdiag/tests/bug-4118.c` has six cases and expects seven errors. Cases 1 to 5 are
functions that use the parameter, and case 6 has two prototypes whose parameters do not have
names. Without the patch the compiler terminates with SIGSEGV in cases 1 to 5 on r17228, and
`valdiag.py` stops at the first of them. With the patch the seven checks pass, and the diagnostics
suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. The regression suite
for mcs51-small has 0 failures, and the code size of every test in it is equal with and without
the patch. The patch does not add a regression test, because it changes only the branches that
report error 198.

## Related

These problems remain with the patch. The compiler does not crash for any of them.

- The check for error 198 requires `IS_SPEC` of the declaration specifiers, so it does not apply
  to parameters whose type is a typedef name of a pointer or function type. With
  `typedef int *P;`, the parameters `constexpr P p`, `static P p`, and `auto P p` compile without
  the error. The `getSpec` check of the ticket's patch reports them. With
  `constexpr int *const cp = 0;`, the parameter `typeof (cp) x` is valid and compiles on r17228.
  It was not tested whether the `getSpec` check reports it.
- `constexpr int c = 3; int f (typeof (c) x) { return x; }` is valid and gets error 198, because
  `typeof` of a `constexpr` object gives a type with the marker. Without the patch the compiler
  also crashes for it. `sizeof (typeof (c))` and `(typeof (c)) v` get error 198 too. The entry
  for #4145 lists this defect of `typeof`.
- `typedef int *P; constexpr P p;` without an initializer and the function definition
  `constexpr int f (void) { ... }` compile without an error.
